title: Reduce streaming token latency: token loop refactor, flush cadence, backpressure, kernel scheduling & KV-cache batching
author: Lena Chen
description: Background: Streaming token generation latency (especially tail/p95) is a frequent customer pain point for real-time experiences. This PR implements a set of coordinated runtime improvements: 1) refactor the token emission loop to reduce scheduler wakes and lock contention; 2) adaptive flush cadence to emit partial buffers earlier under low-latency SLOs while preserving throughput; 3) improved backpressure handling between network readers and the continuous batcher to avoid token stalling under bursty inputs; 4) kernel scheduling hints to prioritize small/interactive streams on MIG and small-GPU instances; 5) batching-aware KV-cache integration so cache hits are propagated without blocking the main token loop. Motivation: incremental changes individually gave modest wins, but combined they remove several micro-latency sources and improve tail behavior without sacrificing throughput. This PR includes benchmarks, integration tests, and a canary rollout plan. Summary of changes: token loop refactor (reduced mutex scope; transition to waiter-notify with per-stream ring buffers), adaptive flush policy (heuristics + a simple PID-ish dampener), backpressure queue with credit accounting in continuous_batcher, kernel_scheduler: add "interactive_priority" path that influences kernel dispatch order and preempts large-batch jobs, kv_cache: add non-blocking lookup path and a fast-path that returns cached KV shards to the batcher; tests: unit tests for flush cadence, integration test for end-to-end streaming with simulated jitter, perf bench harness and canary config. Results: p50 token latency ~ unchanged, p95 improved 18-28% across models we tested (gpt-like small to midsize) and p99 improved up to 35% in low-concurrency canary; throughput stable within 3%. Canary rollout: staged across 5% -> 25% -> 75% -> 100% with automated rollback on error-rate/latency regressions.

review_comments: Oren: Overall this is promising. Two main asks: (1) can you quantify CPU overhead of the fast-path on high-concurrency workloads? (2) please add a short note on how this interacts with existing cache eviction logic.

Lena: replied - added microbench numbers to perf harness and a section in streaming.md; fast-path is <2% CPU at 500 concurrent streams in our test; eviction unchanged as fast-path just returns shard refs and defers eviction to cache manager thread.

Diego: requested change - make the adaptive flush policy opt-in via runtime flag and default to previous behavior for 2 releases. Please add tests for corner cases where flush cadence could increase overhead under heavy batching.
Lena: addressed - added runtime flag --streaming-adaptive-flush (off by default), added flush_cadence_test covering high-batch scenarios and added canary gating.
Maya: approval - verified canary metrics on staging (p95 down ~22%), code looks good; recommend rolling to 25% and verifying for 48h. Approving.
Oren: approving after follow-ups addressed. Merge when CI is green and canary monitors in place.
ci_checks: perf-workflow: pass (benchmarks collected; p95 improved on canary)
perf_results: Model a (small-gpt-like): p50 token latency: 12.4ms -> 12.1ms (2.4%), p95: 48.2ms -> 38.6ms (19.9%), p99: 112ms -> 74ms (33.9%)
Throughput: total tokens/sec within +/-3% under steady-state load (no regression observed)
CPU overhead: fast-path adds <2% CPU at 500 concurrent streams; negligible at high-GPU-utilization hosts
release_notes: Runtime: reduce streaming token generation tail latency by refactoring token loop, adding adaptive flush cadence, improved backpressure in continuous batcher, kernel scheduling hints for interactive streams, and KV-cache non-blocking fast-path. Improves p95/p99 token latency up to ~35% depending on workload. Rolling canary by default; opt-in flag --streaming-adaptive-flush is off by default for two releases.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: deploy to 5% of traffic for 24h, monitor p95/p99 token latency and error-rate
Stage 2: if green, escalate to 25% for 48h and run extended perf harness
Stage 4: 100% while keeping canary monitors for 7 days; automatic rollback on >10% p95 regressions or >1% error rate increase
